title: Production architecture and release-hardening plan
final_sha_source_of_truth: GitHub issue comment after post-commit sync
production_target_architecture: client browser UI -> authenticated API gateway -> tenant/workspace authorization layer -> central application services -> PostgreSQL/search storage -> object/file storage -> async job queue -> observability/backups/migrations
client-agent mediated filesystem access only for approved local operations
admin-only controls remain separate from client workspace controls
gap_analysis: local MVP is validated and reviewable
production authentication and user identity management are still missing
production database and migration strategy are still missing
object storage and backup/restore strategy are still missing
production observability and deployment hardening are still missing
security_and_credentials: control all state-changing operations through backend APIs and workflow checks
keep API keys masked and out of logs/comments
do not expose shell execution or raw credentials in the browser UI
use explicit approval for any filesystem or external-tool execution
migration_plan: introduce PostgreSQL as the production source of truth
add schema versioning and forward-only migrations
move durable uploads/documents to object storage
add backup/restore verification before production rollout
stage migration from local SQLite artifacts to production services
client_agent_strategy: keep filesystem access local and approval-gated
do not allow direct server-side filesystem control
deployment_observability: require health checks and rollback paths
add structured logs, metrics, and audit trails
validate backups, restore drills, and migration dry-runs
phased_sequence: auth, users, tenants, and workspace model
production release gates and preflight validation
immediate_next_task: Create a follow-up Hermes task for auth, users, tenants, and workspace model design plus first PostgreSQL schema and migration outline.
notes: docs/PRODUCTION_HARDENING.md was listed in the task brief but is not present in the repository snapshot.
The local MVP acceptance remains valid and is not equivalent to production readiness.
